intent: Make the design-lint baseline mechanically shrink-only rather than shrink-only by doctrine. Warrant: Q-008 in org/QUESTIONS.md, raised 2026-08-22 by the plan's verification sweep and PROMOTED by the operator the same day; drift finding D-14 in the plan's section 2 is the same fact. The defect: scripts/tooling/design-lint.mjs's --update-baseline writes current counts unconditionally, so running it after a regression grows the baseline, and shrink-only lives in comments and error text rather than in the mechanism. The plan's risk register names baseline grown to absorb violations as an all-phase risk whose only control today is a person comparing totals, and Phases 3, 4 and 5 all re-key baselines. Acceptance: (1) --update-baseline refuses to write a larger total, or a larger per-key count, without an explicit second flag; (2) that second flag carries a written reason and the reason is recorded where the baseline lives; (3) a test plants a regression and proves the refusal, and proves that the second flag with a reason still works; (4) nothing else changes, because the suggestion strengthens a check and touches nothing else. Done when the baseline cannot grow silently, and every phase that re-keys a baseline is protected by mechanism rather than by vigilance. Tier proposal R1, anticipated factor size-threshold from derived signal diff-size if the test fixtures push the diff past the express limits; a single-file change with one test may well route R0 at the gate, in which case this record is the durable trace of a promoted question rather than a ceremony requirement. See T-0018, which builds the same kind of guard for the coverage floors and should share one mechanism. Closed 2026-08-23 in a6cdcd7f. --update-baseline now refuses to write a baseline whose TOTAL or whose count for any SINGLE key is higher than the committed one. The per-key half is the one that matters: two violations cleaned in one file and two added in another leave the total identical, so a totals-only ratchet would wave the regression straight through. The escape hatch needs --allow-growth with at least twelve characters of prose, and the reason is written into the baseline file itself under an append-only __growth__ log, beside the number it excuses. Shape copied deliberately from the coverage ratchet landed the same day, because two gates a person meets in the same week should behave the same way. Review independently planted a violation, watched the refusal, and confirmed the baseline was byte-identical on disk afterwards. Q-008 is answered by mechanism rather than by doctrine.
